subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Write the equation x + y − 2 = 0 in (a) slope-intercept form, (b) intercept form and (c) normal form.

mark_split.label: Divide and read cos α, sin α
Name α and write the normal form

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.158, chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 16(v). **Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work** — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split follows the three parts the question names: two marks for each of the two easy forms, and four for the normal form, which is the only part with a sign condition in it — one for making the right side positive, two for dividing and reading cos α and sin α, and one for naming α. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C prints 3 long answer questions at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Every form was checked back against the original. The slope-intercept form y = −x + 2 rearranges to x + y − 2 = 0; the intercept form x/2 + y/2 = 1 multiplies by 2 to x + y = 2; and the normal form, with cos 45° = 1/√2 and sin 45° = 1/√2, reads x/√2 + y/√2 = √2, which multiplies by √2 back to x + y = 2. The value p = √2 also agrees with the direct perpendicular distance from the origin, |0 + 0 − 2|/√(1² + 1²) = 2/√2 = √2. Note that this line and x + y + 2 = 0 are parallel and equally far from the origin, and their normal angles differ by 180°, which is the expected pattern.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this — name all three forms, and say what condition fixes the angle in the normal form.

steps.label: Slope-intercept form
steps.margin_note: The first two marks. Quote y = mx + c, make y the subject, and then read off m and c separately.
lines: (a) Slope-intercept form is  y = mx + c

recall.must_convey: That making y the subject gives y = −x + 2, so m = −1 and c = 2.
accept: make y the subject to get y equals minus x plus two
slope intercept form is y equals m x plus c
the slope is minus one and c is two
y ni subject ga cheste minus x plus two vasthundi
m equals minus one and c equals two
heard_as: y equals m x plus c

steps.why: Slope-intercept form shows the slope and the y-intercept directly, so the only work is to make y the subject.
common_mistakes: Writing y = −x − 2 by carrying the sign of the constant across wrongly.
steps.memory_tip: y = mx + c: make y the subject, then m is the number in front of x and c is what is left.

steps.label: Intercept form
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. Quote x/a + y/b = 1, move the constant to the right, and divide every term by it.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by 2 gives x/2 + y/2 = 1, so a = b = 2.
accept: move the constant right and divide by two
intercept form is x over a plus y over b equals one
a is two and b is two
constant tho divide chesthe intercept form vasthundi
x over two plus y over two equals one

steps.why: Intercept form must have 1 on the right-hand side, and dividing by the constant is the only way to arrange that.
common_mistakes: Leaving 2 on the right instead of dividing to make it 1.
Dividing only one of the two terms by 2.
steps.memory_tip: x/a + y/b = 1 needs 1 on the right, so divide every term by the constant.

steps.label: Make the right side positive
steps.margin_note: One mark. Normal form carries the condition p > 0. Move the constant across and, if it lands negative, change every sign.
lines: (c) Normal form is  x cos α + y sin α = p,
x + y = 2  already has a positive right side,
so no sign needs to be changed.

recall.must_convey: That the right side is already positive, so no sign change is needed.
accept: the right side is already positive so no sign change
normal form needs p positive
p is a distance so it cannot be negative
right side already positive undi so change avasaram ledu
check the sign of the constant first

steps.why: In normal form p is a perpendicular distance from the origin, so it must be positive, and that single condition is what fixes α.
common_mistakes: Changing every sign anyway, which makes the right side negative.
Not checking the sign of the constant at all before dividing.
steps.memory_tip: p is a distance, so p > 0. Check the sign of the constant before dividing; here it is already positive.

steps.label: Divide and read cos α, sin α
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Divide every term by √(a² + b²), then read cos α, sin α and p off the result in that order.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by √2 gives cos α = 1/√2, sin α = 1/√2 and p = √2.
accept: divide by root two which is root of one plus one
cos alpha and sin alpha are both one over root two
p is root two
root a square plus b square tho divide cheyyali
divide every term by the root of the sum of the squares

steps.why: Dividing by √(a² + b²) makes the two coefficients into a cosine and a sine, because their squares then add to 1.
common_mistakes: Dividing the left side by √2 but not the right.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by √(a² + b²) — the square root of the sum of the squares of the two coefficients.

steps.label: Name α and write the normal form
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Use the signs of cos α and sin α to name the quadrant, then write the finished normal form with the angle in it.
lines: cos α and sin α are both positive, so α lies

recall.must_convey: That both being positive puts α in the first quadrant, so α = 45°.
accept: both are positive so alpha is in the first quadrant
alpha is forty five degrees
x cos forty five plus y sin forty five equals root two
rendu positive so first quadrant, alpha forty five
the related acute angle is forty five

steps.why: The signs of cos α and sin α together name one quadrant, and that is what turns the pair of values into a single angle α.
common_mistakes: Placing α in the third quadrant, where both would be negative.
Leaving the answer as x/√2 + y/√2 = √2 without naming α.
steps.memory_tip: Both cosine and sine positive means the first quadrant, so α is the related acute angle itself.
